title: Quick Sell Tactical Notebook: Ops Rapid Heuristics (variant)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, tactical notebook for SEs and Ops handling short-form pilots and rapid onramps. Meant to be a scratchpad: mix of quick scripts, objection counters, cheap simulations to run during demo/pilot calls, and the emergency fallback phrases to hand over to customers. This variant captures some experimental heuristics we used in the last two pilots and a few unresolved questions to test in the next sprint.

Usage guidance (top of page):
- Read fast: pick 1–2 anchors before the call (latency, cost, fallback).
- Use the canned lines exactly for first pass; personalize after rapport.
- If pilot asks for SLOs, trigger the "pilot-handoff" checklist below and loop in Platform SE.

Snapshot: 2-minute summary to memorize
- Value prop: predictable inference economics + fallbacks that keep UX alive when capacity spikes.
- Fast counters: latency-first demo (sample prompt -> streaming -> fallback to smaller model).
- Pilot metrics to drive: tokens/sec, p95 latency, token cost estimate, false positive rate for hallucination bucket.

Quick scripts and demo flows
1) Latency-first live demo (3–5 min)
   - Start: "We will show a live 512-token generation at p95 under X ms; if anything spikes, we’ll gracefully return a partial answer and re-queue."
   - Demo steps: 
     a) Call hosted API on model "rwrm-large-v1" with stream=true, max_tokens=512, temperature=0.2.
     b) Watch for first-token latency; note time.
     c) On timeout > configured threshold, call fallback policy: route to "rwrm-medium-quant" with truncated prompt + cached prefix.
   - What to say on hiccup: "That looks like a transient throughput spike — we’ll serve the partial result now and re-run the tail on a cheaper variant so your UX stays interactive."

2) Live embedding + rerank micro-pilot (6 min)
   - Use 3 docs sample, 1 user query. Steps: embed docs, embed query, compute cosine, return top-2, then ask follow-up.
   - SE talking points: cache embeddings for static corpora; show cost saving if document set > 10k and cache hit rate > 80%.

Fallback & canary play snippets (copyable)
- Canary trigger rule (ops-friendly pseudo):
  if p95_latency(route) > 2s for 3 consecutive minutes OR error_rate(route) > 0.8% then: set route.fallback = true and alert ops-channel
- Fallback phrasing for customers: "We’re switching to a faster variant to keep response times snappy; quality may vary slightly while we reconcile capacity — full-quality will resume in the background."

Cost-to-value quick math (for call)
- Example pilot estimate (rough):
  - Avg request: 350 tokens input + 350 tokens output = 700 tokens total
  - Hosted unit price (example): $0.0006 per token => $0.42 per request
  - With caching/prefix-sharing (50% saving on output) => ~$0.21 per request
  - Talking cue: "We model cost sensitivity by balancing cache hit-rate vs model size; typically early pilots see 30–50% improvement after caching."

Objection scripts (short)
- Objection: "We can’t tolerate any drop in quality." => Response: "Totally fair — we recommend a canary with A/B where 10% traffic stays on full-quality model and the other 90% uses the fallback; we monitor user-level metrics and roll back automatically if drift detected."
- Objection: "We need predictable bills for finance." => Response: "We can provision a small Dedicated pool and combine reserved capacity pricing with token caps for predictability; I’ll add our finance template to the pilot pack."

Pilot handoff (mini-checklist to file after demo)
- Capture: sample prompt set (10 examples) + expected outputs (gold responses)
- Baseline metrics: p50/p95, cost per request, sample failures with timestamps
- Access: API key with read-only on logs, SAML if needed
- Roles: owner (customer PM), platform SE contact (name/email), ops oncall (channel)
- Timeline: 14-day rapid pilot by default, extend with usage thresholds

Operational heuristics for SEs (notes to self)
- Keep two fallback variants available per account (smaller and quantized).
- If customer uses long-context (>2048 tokens) surface memory / token budget early and suggest split-indexing.
- For high-throughput tests, recommend batch-size tuning: start with conservative batch=4 and increase while measuring p95.

Mini-simulations to run pre-call (scripts you can run in 60–90s)
- Latency smoke: 5 sequential calls, measure first-token and full response, mean and p95.
- Throughput smoke: parallel 12 callers for 60s, measure error rate and queuing.
- Cost smoke: run 20 typical prompts, sum tokens, apply unit pricing to show order-of-magnitude cost.

Example routing policy (talking-level config)
- Priority order: dedicated pool (if available) -> regional hosted -> fallback quantized variant
- Rules: prefer dedicated for enterprise-tier accounts during business hours, else hosted to reduce cost.

Quick triage checklist when pilot breaks (first 5 minutes)
- Check API key and rate limit headers
- Confirm model health dashboard (console) for queue depth and GPU load
- Reproduce a single failing prompt locally with streaming=false to see full stack trace
- If degradation persists, flip route to fallback and notify SE + ops.

Scripting snippets (phrases)
- "I’m going to switch your session to a faster variant so the app stays responsive — you’ll see the full output reprocessed in the background."
- "We’ve got an automated rollback — if quality dips beyond the agreed threshold we’ll revert traffic within minutes."

Open questions & experiments to run (annotated)
- Q1: How often does background reprocessing materially change user satisfaction vs delivering partial-first? Experiment: A/B partial-first vs full-final with NPS follow-up (2-week pilot).
- Q2: Target batching heuristic — can we safely auto-increase batch size for idle accounts during off-peak without violating latency SLOs? Quick sim task for infra team.
- Q3: Quantized fallback calibration — should we tune temperature lower on quantized variants to reduce hallucination frequency? Pilot with 500 prompts.

Risks & mitigation (handy bullets for finance/legal convo)
- Risk: Unexpected token spend during customer load test. Mitigation: put a soft cap and alert cadence; ensure finance has monthly cap override.
- Risk: PII exposure in logs during pilot. Mitigation: enable obfuscation at ingest and share retention policy.

Follow-ups to attach to pilot folder (action items)
- Upload prompt set and labeled outputs to Confluence (owner: Jonah)
- Draft reserved capacity note for finance (owner: Priya)
- Create a short Demo video (2 min) showing fallback in action (owner: Elliot)

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep language blunt and simple — SEs prefer short heuristics rather than long docs.
- If customer wants on-prem, mention Private option but avoid deep-dive until they show monthly spend > $X (threshold to be defined).
- Save a copy of the pilot metrics snapshot at 48h and 14d.

End of notebook. Markers: "TODO: Formalize A/B test template" and "TODO: Define finance spend threshold for Private conversation"

---

- 2026-02-25 updated fallback phrasing and added open experiments (Priya)
